_readme: Mutating routes (POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE) that tools/route-guard-scan.mjs finds
with no authorization middleware between the path and the handler.
Every entry states WHY, using one of three prefixes:
open-by-design: — the route is meant to be callable by any authenticated
user (POS/floor operations, self-service) or by an
unauthenticated caller (public auth handshakes). Not debt.
in-handler:     — authorization IS enforced, inside the handler, where a
middleware-position scanner cannot see it. Not debt, but
the non-standard shape is why the scanner has to be told.
GAP:            — no authorization anywhere. Real debt. Each of these is a
finding in the 2026-08-06 infrastructure audit under
WORK/audits/ and must be closed by adding a guard, not by
reclassifying the entry.
Shrink-only. Adding an entry to silence the scan without one of the three
justifications above is forbidden — that turns a security check back into the
decoration it was before 2026-08-06 (the shell step it replaced could not fail
and had never once evaluated this codebase).
Keys are '<file>:<METHOD> <path>' so entries survive surrounding code moving.
A key that no longer matches an unguarded route fails the scan as STALE —
delete it when the route gains a guard.

routes.src/identity/routes.ts:POST /register: open-by-design: public signup. Brute force is controlled by the dedicated /api/identity/register limiter in app.ts (5 burst, ~3/min).
routes.src/identity/routes.ts:POST /login: open-by-design: public login. There is no token yet to authorize against. Per-IP limiter in app.ts.
routes.src/identity/routes.ts:POST /login/mfa: open-by-design: second leg of public login; carries only a short-lived MFA challenge token.
routes.src/identity/routes.ts:POST /refresh: open-by-design: authorizes on the httpOnly refresh cookie, not a Bearer role.
routes.src/identity/routes.ts:POST /logout: open-by-design: revoking your own session must work even with an expired access token.
routes.src/identity/routes.ts:POST /devices: in-handler: app.ts mounts makeAuthMiddleware on /api/identity/devices; the handler is self-scoped to res.locals.auth.userId.
routes.src/identity/routes.ts:POST /mfa/setup: in-handler: app.ts mounts makeAuthMiddleware on /api/identity/mfa; self-scoped to the calling user.
routes.src/identity/routes.ts:POST /forgot-pass: open-by-design: unauthenticated by definition; the response is uniform so it cannot enumerate accounts.
routes.src/identity/routes.ts:POST /reset-passw: open-by-design: authorizes on the emailed single-use reset token, not a role.
routes.src/modules/billing/routes.ts:POST /bill: GAP: any cashier can create an AP bill. The sibling POST /bills/:id/pay IS mgr-guarded, so money movement is covered but document creation is not.
routes.src/modules/billing/routes.ts:POST /invo: GAP: any cashier can raise an AR invoice against a customer.
routes.src/modules/business/routes.ts:POST /me/: in-handler: service.setActiveBusinessUnit receives the caller's role and enforces which units that role may switch into.
routes.src/modules/catalog/routes.ts:POST /impo: in-handler: rejects any role other than owner/manager. Non-standard shape — it throws badRequest (400) where the rest of the codebase returns 403.
in-handler: same owner/manager check, and the same 400-instead-of-403 shape as POST /import.
routes.src/modules/catalog/routes.ts:POST /: GAP: any cashier can create a product. Every sibling bulk path (/bulk-update, /bulk-price, /bulk-barcodes) is requireRole('manager'); single-product create is not.
routes.src/modules/catalog/routes.ts:POST /:id/: GAP: any cashier can attach a barcode — and therefore a pack-size/UOM conversion (ADR-006) — to a product.
routes.src/modules/catalog/routes.ts:PUT /:id/c: GAP: any cashier can re-categorise a product, which moves it in reporting and in package/mode gating.
routes.src/modules/customers/routes.ts:POST /: open-by-design: creating a customer at the till is a routine cashier action.
routes.src/modules/customers/routes.ts:POST /:i: open-by-design: capturing a delivery address at the till is a routine cashier action.
routes.src/modules/customers/routes.ts:PATCH /:: GAP: correcting an address is plausibly cashier-level, but nothing says so — unlike the contact routes beside it, this carries no capability or role gate at all.
routes.src/modules/customers/routes.ts:DELETE /: GAP: destructive and ungated — a cashier can delete any customer address in the tenant.
routes.src/modules/customers/routes.ts:POST /:i: open-by-design: appending a customer note is a routine cashier action, and notes are append-only.
in-handler: positive deltas (issuing credit) are rejected for cashiers with 403; negative deltas (redeeming at checkout) are allowed.
routes.src/modules/discounts/routes.ts:POST /:i: open-by-design: applying an existing discount at the till is the cashier's job. Creating and editing discounts are mgr-guarded.
routes.src/modules/discounts/routes.ts:POST /ev: open-by-design: pure evaluation against the cart, no persistence.
routes.src/modules/ecommerce/routes.ts:POST /ch: open-by-design: storefront checkout — a customer-facing surface gated as Preview (NEXT_PUBLIC_STORE_AUTH_ENABLED), not by staff role.
routes.src/modules/giftcards/routes.ts:POST /:c: open-by-design: redeeming a gift card at the till is the cashier's job. Issuing is mgr-guarded.
routes.src/modules/inventory/pipeline-routes.ts: GAP: creates a real purchase order from a reorder alert with no role check, while purchasing's own PO routes are mgr-guarded. Inconsistent with the owning module.
GAP: mutates receiving progress with no role check.
routes.src/modules/inventory/routes.ts:POST /de: open-by-design: called automatically by TerminalInner after every cashier-completed sale, with the response deliberately swallowed. Gating it would silently stop stock decrementing rather than fail loudly — documented in the route's own comment.
routes.src/modules/inventory/routes.ts:POST /co: open-by-design: recording counted quantities is floor-staff work; closing the count (which posts variances) is mgr-guarded.
routes.src/modules/notifications/routes.ts:POST: open-by-design: read-state only, tenant-scoped, no business effect.
routes.src/modules/notifications/routes.ts:PATC: open-by-design: read-state only, tenant-scoped, no business effect.
routes.src/modules/orders/routes.ts:POST /: open-by-design: ringing up a sale is the cashier's primary action.
routes.src/modules/orders/routes.ts:PUT /:id: open-by-design: amending an in-progress order at the till. Refunds and voids are separately guarded.
routes.src/modules/orders/routes.ts:POST /:id/e: open-by-design: emailing the customer their own receipt at the till.
routes.src/modules/orders/routes.ts:PATCH /:id/: open-by-design: restaurant coursing, a floor-staff action.
routes.src/modules/orders/routes.ts:POST /:id/s: open-by-design: splitting a bill is a floor-staff action.
routes.src/modules/outlets/routes.ts:POST /: GAP: creating an outlet is a setup action, not a till action — store_locations' equivalents are all mgr-guarded.
routes.src/modules/outlets/routes.ts:POST /:out: GAP: registering a new till is a setup action with no role check.
routes.src/modules/outlets/routes.ts:POST /regi: open-by-design: a cashier taking their own register online/offline.
open-by-design: opening a register with a float is the start of a cashier's shift.
open-by-design: closing and counting down a register ends a cashier's shift; the variance it records is auditable.
routes.src/modules/outlets/routes.ts:POST /shif: open-by-design: cash drops and pickups during a shift, recorded immutably.
routes.src/modules/payments/routes.ts:POST /con: open-by-design: Stripe Terminal reader handshake, needed by every till.
routes.src/modules/payments/routes.ts:POST /ter: open-by-design: starting a card-present payment is the cashier's job.
open-by-design: cancelling an in-flight card prompt at the till.
routes.src/modules/payments/routes.ts:POST /: open-by-design: taking payment is the cashier's primary action. Refunds and voids are separately guarded.
routes.src/modules/permission_requests/routes.t: open-by-design: self-service access request. Approve and revoke are guarded; asking is not.
routes.src/modules/purchasing/routes.ts:POST /r: open-by-design: raising a requisition is deliberately open to any employee — approval is the control point, and the approval routes are guarded.
routes.src/modules/purchasing/routes.ts:PATCH /: open-by-design: editing your own draft requisition before submission.
routes.src/modules/purchasing/routes.ts:POST /r: open-by-design: submitting your own requisition into the approval chain.
routes.src/modules/quotes/routes.ts:POST /: open-by-design: quoting a customer at the counter is a cashier action.
routes.src/modules/quotes/routes.ts:PATCH /:id/: GAP: a cashier can mark any quote accepted, rejected or expired. The module imports no guard at all.
routes.src/modules/quotes/routes.ts:POST /:id/c: GAP: converting a quote creates a real order at quoted prices, with no role check.
routes.src/modules/quotes/routes.ts:DELETE /:id: GAP: destructive and ungated — a cashier can delete any quote in the tenant.
routes.src/modules/restaurant/routes.ts:PATCH /: open-by-design: seating and clearing a table is floor-staff work.
routes.src/modules/restaurant/routes.ts:POST /t: open-by-design: seating a party is floor-staff work.
routes.src/modules/restaurant/routes.ts:POST /s: open-by-design: closing a table session is floor-staff work.
routes.src/modules/restaurant/routes.ts:POST /t: open-by-design: opening a bar tab is floor-staff work.
open-by-design: adding to a tab is floor-staff work.
open-by-design: closing a tab settles through the guarded payment path.
routes.src/modules/restaurant/routes.ts:PATCH /: open-by-design: bumping a kitchen ticket is line-cook work.
routes.src/modules/sales/routes.ts:POST /quotat: open-by-design: B2B quoting at the counter, consistent with quotes POST /.
routes.src/modules/sales/routes.ts:POST /sales-: open-by-design: taking a sales order is a cashier/rep action; fulfilment transitions are guarded.
routes.src/modules/sso/routes.ts:POST /initiate: open-by-design: pre-login OIDC handshake, mounted publicly in app.ts precisely because no token exists yet. Rate-limited like /api/identity.
routes.src/modules/sso/routes.ts:POST /callback: open-by-design: OIDC redirect target. Authorizes on the IdP state/code, not a role.
routes.src/modules/team/routes.ts:POST /: in-handler: requireManagement(res) throws before any service call.
routes.src/modules/team/routes.ts:POST /:id/clo: open-by-design: self-or-management rule enforced in the service; an employee clocking themselves in is the normal case.
open-by-design: same self-or-management rule as clock-in.
routes.src/modules/workforce/routes.ts:POST /ti: open-by-design: requesting your own time off. Approval (PATCH /time-off/:id) is mgr-guarded.
routes.src/modules/workforce/routes.ts:POST /cl: open-by-design: an employee clocking themselves in.
open-by-design: an employee clocking themselves out.
